executor.identity: claude-code opus-5 / solvo qa-executor (dispatched by JB)

cases.instance: edit dialog pre-selects the target's stored role
cases.title: Edit dialog pre-selects the stored role
steps: Sign in as the seeded admin and open the Users page
Click Edit on a user whose stored role is agent
Read the role Select's current value
cases.expected: The role control shows agent — the stored role, not a default or placeholder

cases.instance: promote an agent to admin through the edit dialog
cases.title: Promote agent to admin via the edit dialog
steps: Create an agent through POST /api/users
Open Edit on that user, set role to admin, save
Observe the PUT payload and the Users table row
cases.expected: The PUT carries role=admin, returns 200, the dialog closes and the row shows admin

cases.instance: demote an admin to agent through the edit dialog
cases.title: Demote admin to agent via the edit dialog
steps: Create a user and promote them to admin
Open Edit on that user, set role to agent, save
Observe the PUT payload and the Users table row
cases.expected: The PUT carries role=agent, returns 200 and the row shows agent

cases.instance: the role control offers exactly the two supported roles
cases.title: Role control offers exactly agent and admin
steps: Render the edit form for an existing user
Open the role Select
Enumerate the options
cases.expected: Exactly two options, agent and admin — no blank, no third value

cases.instance: no role control is rendered in create mode
cases.title: Create mode renders no role control
steps: Open the Add User dialog
Inspect the form for a role control
cases.expected: No role Select is present in create mode

cases.instance: an agent cannot reach the Users page to see the role control
cases.title: Agent is kept off the Users page
steps: Sign in as a user whose stored role is agent
Navigate to /users
Observe the redirect and the absence of a Users nav link
cases.expected: The agent is redirected away from /users and sees no Users link

cases.instance: the edit dialog is submitted twice in quick succession
cases.title: Double-submit of the edit dialog
steps: Open Edit on a user and change the role
Trigger save twice before the first response returns
Read the stored role and the table
cases.expected: One effective write; the second submit neither errors visibly nor writes a different role

cases.instance: an authenticated agent calling PUT /api/users/:id directly
cases.title: Agent's direct PUT is refused
steps: Authenticate as an agent via the request fixture
PUT /api/users/<other user id> with a valid role payload
Read the response and the stored role
cases.expected: 403 with the Forbidden body; the target's stored role is unchanged

cases.instance: an unauthenticated caller calling PUT /api/users/:id directly
cases.title: Unauthenticated PUT is refused
steps: Issue PUT /api/users/<id> with no session cookie
Read the response and the stored role
cases.expected: 401; the target's stored role is unchanged

cases.instance: an agent attempting to promote themselves through the API
cases.title: Agent self-promotion is refused
steps: Authenticate as an agent
PUT /api/users/<own id> with role=admin
Read the response and the stored role
cases.expected: 403; the caller's stored role is still agent

cases.instance: a refused non-admin request leaves the stored role unchanged
cases.title: Refused non-admin requests persist nothing
steps: Run each of the three refusal paths above
After each, read the target user back through an admin session
cases.expected: Every refusal is paired with a read proving the stored role did not move

cases.instance: an unsupported role value is rejected
cases.title: Unsupported role value rejected
steps: As admin, PUT /api/users/<id> with role='superadmin'
Read the response and the stored role
cases.expected: 400; nothing written

cases.instance: the role key omitted from the payload is rejected
cases.title: Omitted role key rejected (D1)
steps: As admin, PUT /api/users/<id> with name and email but no role key
Read the response and the stored role
cases.expected: 400; nothing written — role is required on updateUserSchema

cases.instance: a supported role in the wrong case is rejected
cases.title: Wrong-case role rejected
steps: As admin, PUT /api/users/<id> with role='Admin'
Read the response and the stored role
cases.expected: 400 — z.enum is case-sensitive; nothing written

cases.instance: a null role is rejected
cases.title: Null role rejected
steps: As admin, PUT /api/users/<id> with role=null
Read the response and the stored role
cases.expected: 400; nothing written

cases.instance: a request rejected on another field writes no role
cases.title: Rejection on another field writes no role
steps: As admin, PUT with a valid role and an invalid email
Read the response and the stored role
cases.expected: 400; the role did not move even though it was itself valid

cases.instance: a request rejected on an email conflict writes no role
cases.title: 409 email conflict writes no role
steps: As admin, PUT with a valid role change and an email already held by another user
Read the response and the stored role
cases.expected: 409; the role did not move

cases.instance: a role of the wrong JSON type is rejected
cases.title: Wrong-typed role rejected
steps: As admin, PUT role as each of: array, object, integer, boolean
Read each response and the stored role
cases.expected: 400 for every shape; nothing written

cases.instance: a whitespace-padded role string is rejected
cases.title: Padded role string rejected
steps: As admin, PUT role=' admin '
Read the response and the stored role
cases.expected: 400 — no trimming before the enum check; nothing written

cases.instance: unknown keys in the payload are stripped rather than rejected
cases.title: Unknown payload keys are stripped, not refused
steps: As admin, PUT a valid payload plus unknown keys
Read the response and the stored row for any effect of those keys
cases.expected: 200, the unknown keys silently stripped and nothing extra written — updateUserSchema has no .strict() by decision

cases.instance: the $transaction throws part-way through the role write
cases.title: Role write abandoned when the transaction throws
steps: Inject a fault so prisma.$transaction rejects during the PUT
Issue a valid role change
Read the stored role and the target's session rows
cases.expected: Nothing persisted — no role change and no session deletion — and the caller sees a 500

cases.instance: a demoted admin's live session is refused on its next admin request
cases.title: Demoted admin's live session stops authorizing
steps: Sign in as admin A in context 1 and as admin B in context 2
B demotes A to agent
A issues GET /api/users on the same session
cases.expected: 401 — A's session rows were dropped in the same transaction as the role write

cases.instance: a non-demoting save leaves the target's live session authorized
cases.title: Non-demoting save keeps the session alive
steps: Sign in as admin A in context 1 and as admin B in context 2
B saves A's row without changing A's role
A issues an admin-only request
cases.expected: A's session still resolves; an unrelated refusal reads 403, never 401 — the narrow side of the demoted condition

cases.instance: demotion drops every session the demoted user holds, not only the observed one
cases.title: All of a demoted user's sessions are dropped
steps: Sign the same user in from three independent contexts
Demote that user from a separate admin session
Issue a request from each of the three contexts
cases.expected: All three are refused — deleteMany is not scoped to the observed session

cases.instance: demoting a user who holds no live session
cases.title: Demotion with no live session
steps: Create an admin who has never signed in
Demote them
Read the response and the stored role
cases.expected: 200 and the role moves; the empty session deleteMany is a no-op rather than an error

cases.instance: a request already in flight from the target when the demotion commits
cases.title: In-flight request racing the demotion
steps: Start a slow admin-only request as the target user
Commit the demotion from another admin session while it is in flight
Observe which side of the transaction boundary the in-flight request lands on
cases.expected: A characterised, stated outcome — either the pre-demotion or post-demotion answer, not an inconsistent mix

cases.instance: a failed role write leaves the target's session rows intact
cases.title: Failed write does not orphan the session drop
steps: Inject a fault so the user.update inside the transaction fails
Issue a demotion
Read the stored role and the target's session rows
cases.expected: Role unchanged AND sessions intact — the two halves cannot disagree

cases.instance: the database is unavailable when the role change is submitted
cases.title: Role change with the database down
steps: Stop the helpdesk_test database
Issue a valid role change as admin
Restart the database and read the stored role and session rows
cases.expected: A 5xx surfaced to the caller, nothing persisted, and no session dropped

cases.instance: a promoted agent's live session gains admin access without re-login
cases.title: Promoted agent's live session gains admin access
steps: Sign in as an agent in context 1 and as an admin in context 2
The admin promotes the agent to admin
The promoted user issues GET /api/users on the same session
cases.expected: 200 — requireAdmin reads the role fresh from the User row, no re-login needed

cases.instance: promotion leaves the promoted user's sessions intact
cases.title: Promotion does not drop sessions
steps: Promote a signed-in agent from another admin session
Reuse the promoted user's original session
cases.expected: The original session still resolves — the session drop is demotion-only

cases.instance: the promoted user's UI gains the Users nav link without a reload
cases.title: Promoted user's UI reflects the new role
steps: Keep a promoted user's browser context open on a non-Users page
Promote them from another admin session
Observe the nav without a manual reload
cases.expected: A characterised answer: whether the Users link appears without a reload, and if not, what the user must do

cases.instance: promoting a user who is already admin
cases.title: Promotion of an existing admin is a no-op
steps: As admin, PUT role=admin on a user whose stored role is already admin
Read the response, the stored role and the target's sessions
cases.expected: 200, role unchanged, sessions untouched — demoted is false so nothing is dropped

cases.instance: POST /api/users creates a user with role agent
cases.title: Creation still yields an agent
steps: As admin, POST /api/users with name, email and password
Read the created user's role
cases.expected: 201 and role=agent — Role.agent is hardcoded in the create path

cases.instance: POST /api/users ignores a role supplied in the body
cases.title: Supplied role ignored on creation
steps: As admin, POST /api/users with role='admin' in the body
Read the created user's role
cases.expected: 201 and role=agent — createUserSchema does not accept role

cases.instance: the create flow offers no role selection in the UI
cases.title: No role selection on the create path
steps: Open the Add User dialog and complete it
Inspect the POST payload
cases.expected: No role control offered and no role key in the POST body

cases.instance: POST /api/users with an explicitly null role
cases.title: Null role on creation
steps: As admin, POST /api/users with role=null in the body
Read the response and the created role
cases.expected: Creation succeeds with role=agent, the key stripped rather than validated

cases.instance: DELETE on a user whose stored role is admin is refused
cases.title: Stored admin cannot be deleted
steps: As admin, DELETE /api/users/<id of a user whose stored role is admin>
Read the response and whether deletedAt was set
cases.expected: 403 and the row is not soft-deleted

cases.instance: DELETE is permitted once that user has been demoted
cases.title: Demote-then-delete is permitted
steps: Demote an admin to agent
DELETE that user
Read the response and deletedAt
cases.expected: 200 and the row is soft-deleted — the guard reads the currently stored role, by design

cases.instance: a promoted agent becomes protected from deletion
cases.title: Promotion confers deletion protection
steps: Promote an agent to admin
DELETE that user
Read the response and deletedAt
cases.expected: 403 — the protection follows the stored role in both directions

cases.instance: a DELETE racing a promotion of the same user
cases.title: DELETE racing a promotion
steps: Issue DELETE and a promoting PUT on the same user in parallel from two admin sessions
Read the final stored role and deletedAt
cases.expected: A characterised end state — not a soft-deleted admin that neither path will now accept

cases.instance: the users table shows the persisted role after a promotion
cases.title: Table reflects a promotion
steps: Promote a user through the dialog
Read the table row and the stored role independently
cases.expected: The row shows admin and matches the stored role with no manual correction

cases.instance: the users table shows the persisted role after a demotion
cases.title: Table reflects a demotion
steps: Demote a user through the dialog
Read the table row and the stored role independently
cases.expected: The row shows agent and matches the stored role

cases.instance: GET /api/users returns the persisted role for both variants
cases.title: List endpoint returns the canonical role
steps: After a promotion and after a demotion, GET /api/users as admin
Compare each role to the stored row
cases.expected: The endpoint's role matches the stored role in both cases

cases.instance: two rows changed in quick succession both repaint
cases.title: Two role changes in quick succession both repaint
steps: Change the role on two different rows in immediate succession
Observe the table after the ['users'] invalidation settles
cases.expected: Both rows show their new roles; neither is left stale

cases.instance: an edit submitted from a dialog opened before another admin changed the same user
cases.title: Stale edit dialog overwrites a concurrent change
steps: Open the edit dialog on a user in one admin session
Change that user's role from a second admin session
Save the first, now-stale dialog and read the stored role
cases.expected: A characterised outcome — the stale dialog's role wins silently, and that is stated rather than discovered later

cases.instance: the password write throws after the role write has committed
cases.title: Partial write: role committed, password not
steps: Inject a fault so hashPassword rejects
Submit a save carrying both a role change and a password
Read the stored role and whether the old password still authenticates
cases.expected: The divergence is characterised: the password update sits outside the $transaction, so the role change survives a failed password write

cases.instance: promotion is covered by an asserting automated scenario
cases.title: Promotion has asserting automated coverage
steps: Resolve the AC1/AC8 describe from bunx playwright test --list
Read the assertions, not the test names
cases.expected: A scenario asserts the promoted role on both the response and a follow-up read

cases.instance: demotion is covered by an asserting automated scenario
cases.title: Demotion has asserting automated coverage
steps: Resolve the describe from the test list
Read the assertions
cases.expected: A scenario asserts the demoted role on both the response and a follow-up read

cases.instance: direct non-admin API attempts are covered
cases.title: Direct non-admin attempts have automated coverage
steps: Resolve the AC2 describe
Read the status and body assertions
cases.expected: Authenticated-agent, unauthenticated and self-promotion attempts are each asserted

cases.instance: invalid role input is covered
cases.title: Invalid role input has automated coverage
steps: Resolve the AC3 describe
Read the assertions
cases.expected: Unsupported, omitted, wrong-case and null are each asserted with a persistence read

cases.instance: active-session behaviour after demotion is covered
cases.title: Post-demotion session behaviour has automated coverage
steps: Resolve the AC4 describe
Read the assertions on both sides of the condition
cases.expected: Both the 401 side and the 403 side are asserted

cases.instance: creation remaining agent is covered
cases.title: Creation policy has automated coverage
steps: Resolve the AC6 describe
Read the assertions
cases.expected: Both the plain create and the supplied-role create assert role=agent

cases.instance: preservation of admin deletion protection is covered
cases.title: Admin deletion protection has automated coverage
steps: Resolve the AC7 describe
Read the assertions
cases.expected: The 403 on a stored admin and the permitted delete after demotion are both asserted

cases.instance: every negative scenario is paired with a persistence read
cases.title: Negative scenarios are paired with persistence reads
steps: Enumerate every negative scenario in the Role management describe
Confirm each is followed by a read proving nothing was written
cases.expected: The pairing holds for all of them — the pattern this story established and the case set must preserve

cases.instance: edit-mode component assertions still pass with role required
cases.title: Edit-mode component regression
steps: cd client && bun run test
Read the UserForm edit-mode PUT assertions
cases.expected: All edit-mode submit assertions pass in their reshaped form

cases.instance: create-mode component assertions are unaffected
cases.title: Create-mode component regression
steps: cd client && bun run test
Read the create-mode cases
cases.expected: Unchanged and passing — a change here would mean createUserSchema was touched and AC6 is broken

cases.instance: the delete button remains absent on admin rows
cases.title: Role-conditional UI regression
steps: cd client && bun run test
Read the delete-button case for admin rows
cases.expected: No delete button on admin rows — the only pre-existing test of role-conditional UI

cases.instance: the auth guard suite is untouched by this story
cases.title: Auth guard suite regression
steps: Run e2e/tests/auth.spec.ts
Compare to the pre-story baseline
cases.expected: All 31 pass — a failure means the middleware was modified, which the spec says not to do

cases.instance: the pg-boss queue reset keeps the ticket and webhook suites green
cases.title: Job-queue reset regression
steps: Run the full E2E suite from a cold database more than once
Record the run count and the pending/failed job counts
cases.expected: ticket-detail and webhook-inbound-email stay green across repeated runs; pgboss.queue is never truncated

cases.instance: an existing integration that PUTs without role now fails closed
cases.title: Breaking change: role is required on PUT
steps: Replay a pre-GH-8 shaped PUT body — name and email, no role
Read the response and the stored role
cases.expected: 400 and nothing written — the endpoint's contract broke deliberately rather than preserving the stored role

cases.instance: an admin changing their own role is refused
cases.title: Self role change refused
steps: As admin, PUT /api/users/<own id> with the other role
Read the response and the stored role
cases.expected: 403 and the caller's role is unchanged

cases.instance: the self-role refusal is ordered before the email-uniqueness conflict
cases.title: Guard ordering: 403 before 409
steps: As admin, PUT own id with a changed role AND an email already held by another user
Read the status code
cases.expected: 403, not 409 — the self-role guard precedes the uniqueness check

cases.instance: the self-role refusal is surfaced in the edit dialog
cases.title: Self-change refusal surfaced in the UI
steps: As admin, open Edit on your own row, change the role, save
Observe the dialog
cases.expected: The refusal is shown in the dialog rather than failing silently or closing on an error

cases.instance: an admin saving their own row without changing role succeeds
cases.title: Self-save with an unchanged role
steps: As admin, open Edit on your own row, change only the name, save
Read the response
cases.expected: 200 — the guard fires on a role change, not on any self-edit

cases.instance: two admins demoting each other inside one request window
cases.title: Mutual demotion reaching zero admins
steps: Sign in as two admins
Issue both demoting PUTs inside one request window
Count the remaining admins and establish what operator recovery exists
cases.expected: How easily zero admins is reached in practice, and the recovery path, are both characterised and severity-rated

cases.instance: ten parallel alternating role writes on one user
cases.title: Parallel alternating role writes
steps: Issue ten alternating promote/demote writes on one user in parallel
Read every response and the final stored role
cases.expected: No deadlock and a coherent final state

cases.instance: the 401-versus-403 outcome pins both sides of the demoted condition
cases.title: Both sides of the demoted condition are pinned
steps: Exercise a demoting save and read the target's next request status
Exercise a non-demoting save and read the target's next request status
cases.expected: 401 on the demoting side and 403 on the non-demoting side — broadening the condition must fail a test

cases.instance: PUT against a user id that does not exist
cases.title: Unknown user id on PUT
steps: As admin, PUT /api/users/<nonexistent id> with a valid payload
Read the response
cases.expected: 404 — the target lookup precedes every guard

exploratoryCharters.text: CHARTER: explore authorization and session transitions with two independently-authenticated browser contexts and a principal created through POST /api/users to discover privilege retention after demotion or privilege denial after promotion.

CHARTER: explore the create, edit and delete user flows as the seeded admin against a roster containing both roles to discover regressions caused by role becoming a required field on the PUT contract.

CHARTER: explore PUT and DELETE on /api/users/:id with crafted payloads and mismatched identities using Playwright's request fixture to discover authorization bypasses, mass assignment and validation escapes.

exploratoryCharters.area: role writes on principals that cannot sign in
exploratoryCharters.text: CHARTER: explore role mutation on the two principal kinds GET /api/users excludes — soft-deleted rows filtered out by deletedAt, and the protected AI pseudo-user filtered out by id — with a seeded admin driving PUT and DELETE /api/users/:id against each kind separately, to discover unintended privilege state, divergent end states and lost deletability on principals the manageable-user path never shows.

exploratoryCharters.area: concurrent role writes and the admin floor
exploratoryCharters.text: CHARTER: explore concurrent and interleaved role writes across multiple admin sessions to discover whether the roster can reach zero admins and what recovery exists if it does.
